catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 2 results in females
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline data were reported from an open-label Phase 2 trial (Study 207) of an extended-release oral minoxidil in women with mild-to-moderate pattern hair loss. Participants showed robust increases in non-vellus target area hair counts and high rates of improvement on AAIRS, with no treatment-related SAEs and no cardiac AESIs. The results support a favorable efficacy and safety profile and strengthen the rationale for registrational development in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Veradermics, Incorporated (NYSE:MANE), a dermatologist-founded, late-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative therapeutics for pattern hair loss, today announced positive topline results from its open-label Phase 2 clinical trial (Study ‘207’) evaluating VDPHL01, a proprietary extended-release oral minoxidil formulation, in females with mild-to-moderate pattern hair loss. In the study, VDPHL01 achieved consistent hair growth on the endpoint of non-vellus TAHC and patient reported outcome (PRO) benefits of ‘improved’ or ‘much improved’ on the Androgenetic Alopecia Impact Rating Scale (AAIRS) at Month 6. Participants achieved an average increase in non-vellus hair count of 22.7 hairs/cm² and 23.3 hairs/ cm² in once daily and twice daily VDPHL01 treatment arms, respectively. Additionally, 88.9% of participants in the once daily dose arm and 90.0% of participants in the twice daily dose arm achieved ‘improved’ or ‘much improved’ hair coverage on the AAIRS. Treatment with VDPHL01 was generally well tolerated through Month 6 with an overall safety profile consistent with prior studies with VDPHL01. No treatment-related SAEs and no AESIs of cardiac origin were observed in this study.

catalyst_text: Reported positive topline results from Phase 2/3 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from Part A of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 Study ‘302’ in over 500 males with mild-to-moderate pattern hair loss were previously shared. These results mark meaningful clinical progress for the program and support continued late-stage development in this indication.

catalyst_text: Trial met primary and key secondary endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results were reported from Part A of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 519 males with mild-to-moderate pattern hair loss, showing superiority versus placebo. The study met all primary and key secondary endpoints, including TAHC and patient-reported AAIRS improvement, with a generally well tolerated safety profile, supporting advancement in this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: Veradermics, Incorporated (NYSE:MANE), a dermatologist-founded, late-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative therapeutics for pattern hair loss, today announced positive topline results from Part A of its randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 clinical trial (Study ‘302') evaluating VDPHL01, a proprietary extended-release oral minoxidil formulation, in over 500 males with mild-to-moderate pattern hair loss. The trial met all primary and all key secondary endpoints with statistical significance, demonstrating a potentially differentiated clinical profile defined by rapid onset of activity, consistent response across patients, and robust increases in hair count while being generally well tolerated with no treatment-related serious adverse events (SAEs) and no adverse events of special interest (AESIs) of cardiac origin. In the study, VDPHL01 achieved superior hair growth compared with placebo (p<0.0001) on the co‑primary endpoints of non-vellus Target Area Hair Count (TAHC) and patient reported outcome (PRO) benefit of ‘improved' or ‘much improved' on the Androgenetic Alopecia Impact Rating Scale (AAIRS) at Month 6.
